The causal order is: loss/reduction of ESR1 (or of the bound regulatory element) → decreased ESR1 occupancy and coactivator recruitment at the MMP17 promoter/enhancer → reduced RNA polymerase II initiation and elongation at the MMP17 gene → lower MMP17 mRNA, and consequently lower secreted MMP17 protein. Because the comparison is against a matched unperturbed control in the same cellular context, the only variable changed is the ESR1-dependent regulatory input, so the expected direction is a decrease rather than an increase; any compensatory or indirect feedback would have to override this direct loss of activation, which is not the primary expectation. Hence MMP17 expression is expected to go down.
